headline: State official clarifies '4% cut' is actually just a mandatory 'inconvenience fee' for keeping the file on a desk with a nice view
body: The state minister confirmed today that the requested percentage is strictly for 'aesthetic maintenance' of office stationery and premium desk-side chai service. Applicants are encouraged to round up to the nearest whole number to ensure their paperwork remains in the 'priority sunlight' pile.
caption: Efficiency is just a matter of perspective (and commission). Would you pay extra for a document to be processed with a better view? #Governance #AdministrativeFees #TransparentGov (satire)
igHook: Would you pay a premium just to have your file sit on a desk with a better view?
imagePrompt: A cluttered government office desk covered in stacks of dusty paper files, featuring a single ceramic tea cup and an antique rotary telephone.

sourceHeadline.title: ‘Give Me 2%, 3%, 4%’: Annamalai's Big Corruption Claim Against Vijay Govt Ministers

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 8 provides the most vivid, specific, and absurdly human detail ('priority sunlight' pile and 'aesthetic maintenance' of chai service) which elevates it above the repetitive 'app-launching' trope seen in the other entries. It successfully uses deadpan administrative logic to justify corruption without relying on tech-slop cliches.
